items.front: Circular economy — what three things does it reduce?
items.back: Reduces raw-material input, production wastage AND GHG emissions (vs linear 'take-make-dispose'). Reduce–reuse–recycle.

items.front: Negative externality & tragedy of the commons — one line each.
items.back: Externality: social cost > private cost → polluting good overproduced. Tragedy of the commons (Hardin, 1968): open-access shared resources are overused. EKC = inverted-U of income vs degradation.
Pigouvian tax = tax equal to marginal external cost. Cap-and-trade = cap emissions + trade permits (least-cost cuts). Coase: clear property rights + low bargaining cost → efficiency, no regulation.

items.front: Polluter-pays & precautionary principles — legal basis in India?
items.back: Read into Article 21; upheld in Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996). Precautionary: scientific uncertainty is no reason to delay preventive action.

items.front: Environmental law chronology & the umbrella Act.
items.back: Wildlife 1972 → Water 1974 (created CPCB/SPCBs) → Forest Conservation 1980 → Air 1981 → Environment (Protection) Act 1986 (umbrella, post-Bhopal). NGT 2010; EIA Notification 2006.

items.front: BRSR — who mandates it and what kind of disclosures?
items.back: Mandated by SEBI (not RBI) for top-1000 listed companies; disclosures are largely non-financial (ESG). Classic UPSC-2025 SEBI-vs-RBI trap.
items.examPoint: Carbon Markets & Green Finance in India

items.front: Carbon credit = ? Do carbon markets transfer resources to the State?
items.back: 1 carbon credit = 1 tonne CO₂-equivalent. Carbon markets transfer resources among private actors — NOT from private sector to the State. India's CCTS 2023 under Energy Conservation Act (BEE).
items.examPoint: Carbon Markets & Green Finance in India

items.front: Green hydrogen decarbonises which heavy industries?
items.back: Fertilizer plants, oil refineries AND steel plants (all three). National Green Hydrogen Mission 2023 (electrolysis with renewables).

items.back: WTO agriculture subsidy category (non-distorting support) — NOTHING to do with the environment. A recurring UPSC distractor alongside amber/blue boxes.

items.front: PAGE and District Mineral Foundation — purpose?
items.back: PAGE (Partnership for Action on Green Economy) launched at Rio+20 (2012), UNEP-led. DMF (MMDR Amendment 2015, funded by PMKKKY) protects interests of persons affected by mining.

items.front: Kyoto vs Paris; what is REDD+?
items.back: Kyoto Protocol 1997 → CDM, JI, ETS. Paris 2015 → NDCs, Art 6 market mechanisms. REDD+ = reducing emissions from deforestation & forest degradation (forest carbon, UNFCCC).
items.examPoint: India's Climate Commitments — Paris, Panchamrit & Net-Zero

items.front: India's Panchamrit net-zero year & key 2030 targets.
items.back: Net-zero by 2070. Panchamrit (COP26, 2021): 500 GW non-fossil, 50% renewables, 45% intensity cut (vs 2005), 1 billion-tonne emission cut. NDC 2022: 45% intensity, ~50% non-fossil power.
items.examPoint: India's Climate Commitments — Paris, Panchamrit & Net-Zero

items.front: Green GDP and coal nationalisation/allocation facts.
items.back: Green GDP = NDP − depletion of natural capital (SEEA; EnviStats since 2018). Coal nationalised 1971-73; blocks now via auction (not lottery); India imports coking coal. GM food imports need GEAC nod.
